10.1002_adfm.78908: Selective CO 2 ‐to‐formate electroreduction requires oxygen‐deficient SnO x sites that stabilize O‐bound * OCHO intermediates while resisting cathodic over‐reduction. Here, we use a precursor‐level coordination competition strategy to construct an oxygen vacancy (O v )‐rich SnO x catalyst coupled with isolated Cu–N sites through controlled conversion of amino‐functionalized Cu/Sn metal‐organic frameworks. Competitive coordination of Cu and Sn with 2‐aminoterephthalic acid (H 2 BDC‐NH 2 ) is associated with altered precursor growth and a heterogeneous local environment, favoring the formation of defective SnO x domains during thermal conversion while enabling ligand‐derived nitrogen sites to anchor redistributed Cu species. Spectroscopic investigations reveal that the optimized Cu‐SnO x /NC catalyst contains abundant vacancy‐related SnO x environments and predominantly isolated Cu–N configurations, which are associated with stabilized O‐bound * OCHO intermediates and mitigated cathodic reconstruction of SnO x . Operando Raman spectroscopy further indicates persistent formate‐related intermediates and comparatively lower bicarbonate accumulation during CO 2 electroreduction. Consequently, Cu‐SnO x /NC achieves a formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96% at −100 mA cm −2 and maintains efficiencies above 85% over a moderate current density range in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes. Half‐cell and full‐cell energy efficiencies (EE) of 65% and 54%, respectively, were achieved in the flow cell and membrane electrode assembly (MEA). This work provides a coordination‐competition strategy for durable high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction.
10.1016_j.solmat.2026.114548: Pristine SnO 2 electron transport layer (ETL) constrains planar perovskite solar cells (PSCs) performance due to poor crystallinity, misaligned energetics, low wettability, and limited conductivity. Here, conductive Mo 3 C 2 T x MXene (MX) nanoflakes with tunable surface chemistry and excellent interfacial compatibility are incorporated into SnO 2 to overcome these limitations. MX incorporation enhances the crystallinity and conductivity of SnO 2 while effectively tuning its work function and improving surface wettability. These improvements promote the formation of high-quality perovskite films with enhanced interfacial contact and reduced defect density. Furthermore, optimized work-function alignment and increased conductivity facilitate more efficient charge extraction and transport, as confirmed by steady-state photoluminescence, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and dark J–V measurements. As a result, PSCs based on MX-SnO 2 achieve a superior power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.16%, outperforming pristine SnO 2 -based devices (PCE = 18.02%). Moreover, the MX-SnO 2 devices maintain 95.1% of its initial efficiency after 42 days at 25 °C under the 40–60% humidity. These findings demonstrate that MXene modification in ETLs is an effective strategy for enhancing the efficiency and stability of PSCs.
10.1038_s41467-026-68481-6: Electrochemical CO2 and nitrite co-reduction provides a sustainable urea synthesis route but remains limited by low selectivity and an undecided C–N coupling mechanism. Here, we report co-sputtered bimetallic Cu–Co catalysts that facilitate urea formation via a tandem relay mechanism. The optimal Cu:Co ratio of 1:1 achieves a urea yield rate of 61 ± 6 mmol h⁻1gcat⁻1 at –1.2 V vs. RHE under neutral pH, emphasizing the importance of proton balance in sustaining proton-coupled electron transfer. In situ synchrotron-based infrared and Raman spectroscopy monitor the dynamic evolution of *CO, *NH2, and C‒N intermediates. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicates the structural stability of metallic Cu and Co active sites. Density functional theory calculations suggest that *COOH + *NH2 coupling initiates urea pathway, with *NH2CO formation as the potential-determining step. This study integrates rational catalyst design and in situ spectroelectrochemical analysis to advance understanding of electrochemical C–N coupling for urea synthesis. Electrochemical conversion of CO2 and nitrite offers a green route to produce urea. Here, the authors report co-sputtered copper cobalt catalysts enable efficient C–N coupling through a tandem mechanism, yielding 61 mmol h⁻1gcat⁻1 urea at –1.2 V vs. RHE.
